title: Credit, debt and credit scores
examples: What is the difference between credit and debit?
Why is paying bills on time so important?
How does my credit score actually work?

explain.say: Today we are learning about borrowing money and credit.
The cost of borrowing money is called interest.
Paying back borrowed money on time is very important.

items: On Time Payment -> Good Credit History

explain.say: Your credit score is a number that shows lenders your reliability.
A high score means lenders are more likely to trust you.
In real life, when you want to buy a phone, the shop might check your score.

faq.a: Interest is the extra money you pay back to the lender for letting you use their money. It is the cost of borrowing.
asks: What is the cost of a loan?
Do I pay interest on credit cards?

faq.q: Does paying my bills late ruin my score?
faq.a: Yes, missing payments or paying late records negative information on your credit file. This lowers your score significantly.
asks: How long does a late payment affect my score?
What is the worst thing for my credit score?

faq.q: What makes my credit score go up?
faq.a: Using credit responsibly, like paying bills on time and keeping low balances, builds a positive history. This shows lenders you are reliable.
asks: What is the best way to build credit?
Do I need to borrow money to raise my score?

faq.q: Are credit cards always bad for me?
faq.a: Not necessarily; they are tools. If you only use them for things you can afford and pay back fully, they can be useful. Overspending is the real danger.
asks: Should I use a credit card?
What is the difference between credit and debit?

faq.q: If I pay everything back, does my score go up?
faq.a: Paying everything back fully and on time is a major positive factor. It shows you are managing debt well and are trustworthy.
asks: Is paying off debt good for my score?
What is the best payment habit?

facts: Interest is the extra money paid on top of the original loan amount.
Paying bills on time is the single most important habit for a good score.
A credit score is a number that predicts how likely you are to repay debt.
Keeping credit card balances low shows responsible borrowing.

quiz.say: If you borrow ten dollars and pay back twelve dollars, what is the extra amount?
quiz.why: Interest is the extra cost you pay for borrowing the money.

wrong.0: Payment is the total money you give back, including interest.
wrong.2: The principal is only the original amount you borrowed.
wrong.3: The balance is what you owe at one moment in time.

quiz.say: Which action helps build the highest credit score?

options.show: Making all payments by the due date
options.say: Making all payments by the due date

options.show: Ignoring bills until they are very late
options.say: Ignoring bills until they are very late

quiz.why: Consistent, timely payments show lenders you are reliable with money.

wrong.1: Taking out a large loan increases your debt, which can lower your score.
wrong.2: Using credit cards often without paying it off increases your debt load.
wrong.3: Ignoring bills causes severe negative marks on your credit file.

quiz.say: If a lender sees you pay off a debt quickly, they think you are:
quiz.why: Paying debts off quickly shows you manage your money well and are trustworthy.

wrong.0: Instability suggests your income might not be steady enough.
wrong.2: Being desperate suggests you might struggle with future payments.
wrong.3: High risk means the lender expects you to default on payments.
